# Gofo parcel network quickly mushrooms in 2026

Gofo's new Dallas warehouse is twice the size of the previous facility, allowing it to process more parcels while improving efficiency. (Photo: Gofo) 

 Eric Kulisch August 27, 2026 7 min read

Parcel delivery startup Gofo has doubled the capacity of its Dallas processing center after moving into a new building and installing automated sortation equipment, as it races other regional carriers to build national scale. 

The larger terminal comes on line ahead of the peak season rush, allowing the company to absorb greater volume in the central United States rather than adding temporary facilities mid-season. Gofo says it expects parcel volume to jump 50% above normal weekly levels during the period between Thanksgiving and Christmas. 

Gofo inaugurated the new facility, which adds about 200,000 square feet of new space along with a large-scale double-deck cross-belt sorter, last week. The new site has 42 dock doors and can handle up to 45,000 parcels per hour, doubling daily capacity to 800,000 pieces per day, the company said in a news release on Tuesday.

By Josh Croup

Published: Sep. 29, 2026 at 5:28 PM EDT

FINDLAY, Ohio (WTVG) - Sheetz cut the ribbon Tuesday on a new food production and distribution facility in Findlay that is bringing hundreds of new jobs to the area.

The $169 million facility has been five years in the making and will be a key part of the company’s efforts to expand across the Midwest.

“It really enables us for the growth that we have planned,” Sheetz CEO Travis Sheetz said. “We’re growing in Ohio with 140 stores today and many more to come. - September 25, 2026 10:58 am·

By Christina Rosell Quiroz, Hackbarth Delivery Services, Final Mile Solutions & Marketing Manager 

How do you establish reliable service in a state as big as Texas?

If you’re Kelly Picard, you do it all at once.

In 2017, Hackbarth opened 11 Texas terminals simultaneously. In a state where a route that works in Dallas may make little sense in Amarillo, that mattered. Any shipper who has tried to cover Texas with one or two hubs knows how quickly service can thin out between cities.

As CEO and the second generation of the Hackbarth family to lead the business, Kelly knew what the company could do for customers, especially with critical goods in pharmaceutical and medical distribution. Hackbarth has stepped in when shippers needed dependable service since Rob Hackbarth, her father, founded the company in 1975. Kelly saw an opportunity to bring that same reliable service to Texas on a much larger scale.

Wing added Denver and Seattle to the list of metro areas set to receive autonomous aerial delivery in 2027 through a partnership with Walmart, building on what was already slated to be a year of scaling for the Alphabet-owned drone delivery company. 

Wing announced the expansion of drone delivery services to the most populous cities in Washington and Colorado on October 5. # Grip is taking the guesswork out of shipping the cold stuff

 Riley Kaminer September 15, 2026 

For years, shipping perishable goods came with a costly rule of thumb: Send everything overnight, pack in as much coolant and insulation as possible, and hope for the best. Grip founder and CEO Juan Camilo Meisel thinks brands can be far more precise.

“This one box does require these four gel packs and this one service, but this other box, you can actually get away with two gel packs and this other shipment service that’s cheaper,” Meisel [pictured above] told Refresh Miami.

That focus has helped the Miami-based logistics and technology company grow 100% year over year for the past three years. Grip is nearing 200 employees and expanding the physical network behind its software. A new 150,000-square-foot facility in Reno was set to open Sept. 1, while the company has moved into a larger Michigan building and plans further growth in New Jersey and Florida. With five facilities, Grip expects to reach 80% of the U.S. population within 24 hours.
